raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Run the Step-5 CSA prefill indexer scores on the native FP8 MFMA on fnuz GPUs (MI300X/MI325X, gfx942). The ROCm path gets its own kernel in `vllm/models/step5/amd/ops/indexer_scores.py`, and the Hopper `paged_mqa_logits_sm90` in `common/` stays as it is. Follow-up to #61837.

## Claims

- Prefill indexer scoring is 4.6-4.95x faster on MI325X.
- Step-5-Preview serving throughput improves by up to 117% at 128k input on 8x MI325X.
- Numerically equivalent: the FP8 operands are reinterpreted exactly, and the extra factor of 4 is a power of two.
- No shared or NVIDIA code changes.

## Validation

**Setup:** Step-5-Preview, 8x MI325X, TP=8, FP8 KV cache, `--block-size 32`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly. Before is the same container without this change.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --moe-backend triton --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch --no-enable-prefix-caching --reasoning-parser step5 --tool-call-parser step5 --enable-auto-tool-choice --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-processor-cache-type shm --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}'
```

### Kernel

One 4096-row prefill chunk, page size 32. Before is `paged_mqa_logits_sm90`, which the ROCm path used until now. Both match a float64 reference to the same error (3.05e-05).

| Heads | Regions | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 8000 | 17648 us | 3565 us | 4.95x |
| 8 | 16000 | 35227 us | 7156 us | 4.92x |
| 16 | 8000 | 18061 us | 3913 us | 4.62x |
| 16 | 16000 | 36137 us | 7802 us | 4.63x |

### Serving

`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, `--ignore-eos`, one warmup round with a different seed.

| ISL / OSL / conc | Total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k / 1k / 8 | 2571 -> 2636 (+3%) | 3.5 -> 3.0 s | 24.6 -> 24.4 ms |
| 8k / 1k / 64 | 7518 -> 7938 (+6%) | 13.9 -> 12.1 s | 62.9 -> 60.0 ms |
| 64k / 1k / 8 | 4699 -> 7447 (+58%) | 40.5 -> 21.8 s | 71.1 -> 48.4 ms |
| 128k / 1k / 8 | 3423 -> 7418 (+117%) | 122.0 -> 52.8 s | 182.3 -> 87.4 ms |

### Accuracy: GSM8K (lm-eval, 1319 questions, 5-shot, chat completions, same setup as #61837)

| | Strict match | Flexible extract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 96.89 ± 0.48 | 97.12 ± 0.46 |
| After | 96.51 ± 0.51 | 96.89 ± 0.48 |

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --model_args model=stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_length=32768,tokenized_requests=False --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=16384,temperature=0
```

### Tests

New tests in `tests/models/step5/test_amd_csa_indexer_scores.py`:

- `test_scores_match_float64_on_scrambled_pages` compares scrambled page tables against a float64 reference, with `0x80` bytes injected into Q and K.
- `test_scores_exact_on_every_fp8_byte_pair` multiplies every pair of the 254 finite e4m3fn values and expects the exact product, so -0, subnormals and ±448 are covered on both operands.

`pytest tests/models/step5` on MI325X: 31 passed. The 2 failures (`test_select_regions_breaks_ties_by_region_id`, `test_fp8_kv_block_size_32_initializes`) fail the same way without this change, because the nightly image lacks `_C` ops they need.

## Details

The ROCm prefill indexer called `paged_mqa_logits_sm90`, which bitcasts the packed FP8 bytes to `tl.float8e4nv` (OCP e4m3fn). gfx942 MFMA only takes e4m3fnuz, so Triton upcast both operands to f16 in software before the dot, and this kernel became the main prefill cost at long context.

e4m3fnuz has the same bit layout with an exponent bias one higher, so every finite e4m3fn byte read as e4m3fnuz is exactly half its value. The ROCm kernel reads the bytes as `tl.float8e4b8`, runs the native MFMA and multiplies the FP32 dot by 4.

The one byte that differs is `0x80`, which is -0 in e4m3fn but NaN in e4m3fnuz, so it is mapped to `0x00`. The e4m3fn NaN bytes (`0x7f`, `0xff`) would read as finite values, but quantized Q and summary keys never contain NaN.

The ROCm kernel is `paged_mqa_logits_sm90` plus this branch, so the Hopper path is untouched. The branch is a `tl.constexpr` selected by `current_platform.is_fp8_fnuz()`, so gfx950 compiles the same code as before.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Step-5 prefill indexer scores vs a float64 reference on scrambled pages."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.step5.common.ops.sparse_indexer_scores import paged_mqa_logits_sm90
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_rocm() or current_platform.has_device_capability(90)),
+    reason="needs FP8 Triton dot",
+)
+
+DIM = 256
+
+
+def _fp8_bytes(shape: tuple[int, ...]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    raw = torch.randn(shape, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8)
+    # 0x80 is -0 in e4m3fn but NaN in e4m3fnuz.
+    return raw.masked_fill(torch.rand(shape, device="cuda") < 0.01, 0x80)
+
+
+def _reference(q, kv_fused, weights, block_tables, seq_lens, max_seq_len):
+    batch, next_n, heads, _ = q.shape
+    pages, page_size = kv_fused.shape[:2]
+    packed = kv_fused.view(pages, -1)
+    keys = packed[:, : page_size * DIM].view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).double()
+    keys = keys.view(pages, page_size, DIM)
+    scales = packed[:, page_size * DIM :].view(torch.float32).double()
+
+    k = torch.arange(max_seq_len, device=q.device)
+    page = block_tables.long()[:, k // page_size]
+    dots = torch.einsum("bnhd,bkd->bnhk", q.double(), keys[page, k % page_size])
+    w = weights.double().view(batch, next_n, heads, 1)
+    logits = (dots.relu() * w).sum(2) * scales[page, k % page_size][:, None]
+    logits = logits.masked_fill(k >= seq_lens[:, None, None], float("-inf"))
+    return logits.view(batch * next_n, max_seq_len).float()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads", [8, 16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("next_n", [1, 2])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_paged_mqa_logits_sm90(heads: int, next_n: int):

nodes.body:
Great find @akii96! This source changes look good, although like @AndreasKaratzas I was thrown off by the sm90 name.

For the testing, I think we should add a few more tests (especially around the extremal range of the dtype) would be a good safeguard against some nasty bitcast bugs.

This generates inputs using `torch.randn(...).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)`, which only produces values around [-4, 4] (Plus the injected 0x80 bytes). That leaves the upper exponent range of e4m3fn (up to max normal ±448.0 at 0x7e/0xfe) completely untested, and only rarely hits subnormal values (0x01..0x07 / 0x81..0x87).

Could we also test the boundary bytes—specifically min subnormal (0x01/0x81), the subnormal/normal boundary (0x07/0x08), and max finite normal (0x7e/0xfe = ±448.0)?

Alternatively, _fp8_bytes could sample across all valid byte patterns since there are only 254 or scale randn so the test exercises the full dynamic range and confirms there are no underflow/overflow or subnormal-flushing discrepancies on gfx942

I added `test_scores_exact_on_every_fp8_byte_pair` in 38175fcb5. It multiplies every pair of the 254 finite e4m3fn values and checks for an exact match, so -0, the subnormals, the 0x07/0x08 boundary and ±448 are all covered on both sides. It passes on MI325X.

I also moved the kernel to `amd/ops` and renamed the test, as mentioned in my reply to Andreas (would also appreicate your inputs on that as there was a follow up question there). Thanks again!

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""ROCm Step-5 CSA prefill indexer scores vs a float64 reference."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.step5.amd.ops.indexer_scores import paged_mqa_logits
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="Step5 CSA kernels are the ROCm path"
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+DIM = 256
+
+
+def _fp8_bytes(shape: tuple[int, ...]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    raw = torch.randn(shape, device=DEVICE).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8)
+    # 0x80 is -0 in e4m3fn but NaN in e4m3fnuz.
+    return raw.masked_fill(torch.rand(shape, device=DEVICE) < 0.01, 0x80)
+
+
+def _reference(q, kv_fused, weights, block_tables, seq_lens, max_seq_len):
+    batch, next_n, heads, _ = q.shape
+    pages, page_size = kv_fused.shape[:2]
+    packed = kv_fused.view(pages, -1)
+    keys = packed[:, : page_size * DIM].view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).double()
+    keys = keys.view(pages, page_size, DIM)
+    scales = packed[:, page_size * DIM :].view(torch.float32).double()
+
+    k = torch.arange(max_seq_len, device=q.device)
+    page = block_tables.long()[:, k // page_size]
+    dots = torch.einsum("bnhd,bkd->bnhk", q.double(), keys[page, k % page_size])
+    w = weights.double().view(batch, next_n, heads, 1)
+    logits = (dots.relu() * w).sum(2) * scales[page, k % page_size][:, None]
+    logits = logits.masked_fill(k >= seq_lens[:, None, None], float("-inf"))
+    return logits.view(batch * next_n, max_seq_len).float()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads", [8, 16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("next_n", [1, 2])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_scores_match_float64_on_scrambled_pages(heads: int, next_n: int):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    batch, page_size, max_seq_len = 11, 32, 700
+    pages_per_req = -(-max_seq_len // page_size)
+    num_pages = batch * pages_per_req + 5
+    block_tables = (
+        torch.randperm(num_pages, device=DEVICE)[: batch * pages_per_req]
+        .view(batch, pages_per_req)
+        .int()
+    )
+    seq_lens = torch.randint(
+        0, max_seq_len + 1, (batch,), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    scales = torch.rand(num_pages, page_size, device=DEVICE)
+    kv_fused = torch.cat(
+        [_fp8_bytes((num_pages, page_size * DIM)), scales.view(torch.uint8)], dim=1
+    ).view(num_pages, page_size, 1, DIM + 4)
+    q = _fp8_bytes((batch, next_n, heads, DIM)).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    weights = torch.randn(batch * next_n, heads, device=DEVICE)
+    args = (q, kv_fused, weights, block_tables, seq_lens, max_seq_len)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        paged_mqa_logits(*args), _reference(*args), rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3
+    )
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_scores_exact_on_every_fp8_byte_pair():
+    """Each score is one product of two FP8 values, so it is exact in FP32."""
+    codes = torch.arange(256, device=DEVICE).to(torch.uint8)
+    codes = codes[(codes & 0x7F) != 0x7F]  # Drop the NaN codes.

+

+        q.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        kv_fused,
+        weights,
+        block_tables.repeat(n, 1),
+        seq_lens,
+        n,
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Step-5 CSA prefill indexer scores from packed FP8 summary pages on ROCm."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["TABLE_ROW", "REGIONS"])
+def _paged_scores_kernel(
+    Q,
+    KV,
+    W,
+    Lengths,
+    Table,
+    Output,
+    Q_BATCH: tl.constexpr,
+    Q_NEXT: tl.constexpr,
+    Q_HEAD: tl.constexpr,
+    W_ROW: tl.constexpr,
+    W_HEAD: tl.constexpr,
+    KV_PAGE: tl.constexpr,
+    TABLE_ROW,
+    TABLE_COL: tl.constexpr,
+    LENGTH_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    REGIONS,
+    NEXT_N: tl.constexpr,
+    HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    PAGE_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    TILE: tl.constexpr,
+    FNUZ: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    batch = row // NEXT_N
+    region = tl.program_id(1) * TILE + tl.arange(0, TILE)
+    length = tl.load(Lengths + batch * LENGTH_STRIDE)
+    valid = (region < REGIONS) & (region < length)
+    physical = tl.load(
+        Table + batch * TABLE_ROW + (region // PAGE_SIZE) * TABLE_COL,
+        valid,
+        other=0,
+    ).to(tl.int64)
+    d = tl.arange(0, 256)
+    h = tl.arange(0, 16)
+    key = tl.load(
+        KV
+        + physical[:, None] * KV_PAGE
+        + (region % PAGE_SIZE)[:, None] * 256
+        + d[None, :],
+        valid[:, None],
+        other=0,
+    )
+    query = tl.load(
+        Q.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8))
+        + batch * Q_BATCH
+        + (row % NEXT_N) * Q_NEXT
+        + h[None, :] * Q_HEAD
+        + d[:, None],
+        h[None, :] < HEADS,
+        other=0,
+    )
+    if FNUZ:
+        # e4m3fn bits read as e4m3fnuz halve each operand (x4); 0x80 is fnuz NaN.
+        key = tl.where(key == 0x80, 0, key).to(tl.float8e4b8, bitcast=True)
+        query = tl.where(query == 0x80, 0, query).to(tl.float8e4b8, bitcast=True)
+        dot = tl.dot(key, query, out_dtype=tl.float32) * 4.0
+    else:
+        key = key.to(tl.float8e4nv, bitcast=True)
+        query = query.to(tl.float8e4nv, bitcast=True)
+        dot = tl.dot(key, query, out_dtype=tl.float32, max_num_imprecise_acc=0)
+    dot = tl.maximum(dot, 0.0)
+    weights = tl.load(W + row * W_ROW + h * W_HEAD, h < HEADS, other=0)
+    # Match the four independent FP32 FMA chains used by the decode indexer.
+    sums = tl.full((TILE, 4), 0, tl.float32)
+    lane = tl.arange(0, 4)
+    for group in tl.static_range(HEADS // 4):
+        index = group * 4 + lane
+        a = tl.gather(dot, tl.broadcast_to(index[None, :], (TILE, 4)), 1)
+        w = tl.gather(weights, index, 0)
+        sums = tl.fma(a, w[None, :], sums)
+    a = tl.gather(sums, tl.full((TILE, 1), 0, tl.int32), 1).reshape((TILE,))
+    b = tl.gather(sums, tl.full((TILE, 1), 1, tl.int32), 1).reshape((TILE,))
+    c = tl.gather(sums, tl.full((TILE, 1), 2, tl.int32), 1).reshape((TILE,))
+    e = tl.gather(sums, tl.full((TILE, 1), 3, tl.int32), 1).reshape((TILE,))
+    scales = tl.load(
+        (KV + physical * KV_PAGE + PAGE_SIZE * 256 + (region % PAGE_SIZE) * 4).to(
+            tl.pointer_type(tl.float32)
+        ),
+        valid,
+        other=0,
+    )
+    result = (((a + b) + c) + e) * scales
+    tl.store(
+        Output + row * REGIONS + region,
+        tl.where(valid, result, float("-inf")),
+        region < REGIONS,
+    )
+
+
+def paged_mqa_logits(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_fused: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: torch.Tensor,
+    block_tables: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    max_seq_len: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Score packed summary pages: all FP8 keys, then one FP32 scale per key."""
+    batch, next_n, heads, dim = q.shape
+    assert q.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn and dim == 256
+    assert heads in (4, 8, 16) and q.stride(-1) == 1
+    assert kv_fused.dtype == torch.uint8 and kv_fused.is_contiguous()
+    assert kv_fused.shape[2:] == (1, 260)
+    assert weights.shape == (batch * next_n, heads)
+    output = torch.empty(
+        (batch * next_n, max_seq_len), dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device
+    )
+    if batch and max_seq_len:
+        _paged_scores_kernel[(batch * next_n, triton.cdiv(max_seq_len, 32))](
+            q,
+            kv_fused,
+            weights,
+            seq_lens,
+            block_tables,
+            output,
+            *q.stride()[:3],
+            *weights.stride(),
+            kv_fused.stride(0),
+            *block_tables.stride(),
+            seq_lens.stride(0),
+            max_seq_len,
+            next_n,
+            heads,
+            kv_fused.shape[1],
+            32,
+            FNUZ=current_platform.is_fp8_fnuz(),
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+    return output

+"""Step-5 prefill indexer scores vs a float64 reference on scrambled pages."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.step5.common.ops.sparse_indexer_scores import paged_mqa_logits_sm90
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+

+    not (current_platform.is_rocm() or current_platform.has_device_capability(90)),
+    reason="needs FP8 Triton dot",
+)
+
+DIM = 256
+
+
+def _fp8_bytes(shape: tuple[int, ...]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    raw = torch.randn(shape, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8)
+    # 0x80 is -0 in e4m3fn but NaN in e4m3fnuz.
+    return raw.masked_fill(torch.rand(shape, device="cuda") < 0.01, 0x80)
+
+
+def _reference(q, kv_fused, weights, block_tables, seq_lens, max_seq_len):
+    batch, next_n, heads, _ = q.shape
+    pages, page_size = kv_fused.shape[:2]
+    packed = kv_fused.view(pages, -1)
+    keys = packed[:, : page_size * DIM].view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).double()
+    keys = keys.view(pages, page_size, DIM)
+    scales = packed[:, page_size * DIM :].view(torch.float32).double()
+
+    k = torch.arange(max_seq_len, device=q.device)
+    page = block_tables.long()[:, k // page_size]
+    dots = torch.einsum("bnhd,bkd->bnhk", q.double(), keys[page, k % page_size])
+    w = weights.double().view(batch, next_n, heads, 1)
+    logits = (dots.relu() * w).sum(2) * scales[page, k % page_size][:, None]
+    logits = logits.masked_fill(k >= seq_lens[:, None, None], float("-inf"))
+    return logits.view(batch * next_n, max_seq_len).float()
+
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("next_n", [1, 2])
+@torch.inference_mode()

inline_comments.body:
This generates inputs using `torch.randn(...).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)`, which only produces values around [-4, 4] (Plus the injected 0x80 bytes). That leaves the upper exponent range of e4m3fn (up to max normal ±448.0 at 0x7e/0xfe) completely untested, and only rarely hits subnormal values (0x01..0x07 / 0x81..0x87).

Could we also test the boundary bytes—specifically min subnormal (0x01/0x81), the subnormal/normal boundary (0x07/0x08), and max finite normal (0x7e/0xfe = ±448.0)?

Alternatively, _fp8_bytes could sample across all valid byte patterns since there are only 254 or scale randn so the test exercises the full dynamic range and confirms there are no underflow/overflow or subnormal-flushing discrepancies on gfx942

I added `test_scores_exact_on_every_fp8_byte_pair` in 38175fcb5. It multiplies every pair of the 254 finite e4m3fn values and checks for an exact match, so -0, the subnormals, the 0x07/0x08 boundary and ±448 are all covered on both sides. It passes on MI325X.
